sections.text: Those who always act in accordance with My precepts, firm in faith and without cavilling, they too are freed from the bondage of action.
But they who ridicule My word and do not keep it, are ignorant, devoid of wisdom and blind. They seek but their own destruction.
Even the wise man acts in character with his nature; indeed, all creatures act according to their natures. What is the use of compulsion then?

So we had been discussing chapter three, Karma Yoga, Yoga of Action. So we have seen in last few verses. Bhagavan says that Prakrute, he, kriyamanani, gunaihi, karmani, sarvasa, all actions are performed by Prakriti.
Ahankara, vimu, dhatma, karta, aham ithimanyade. But the one who is deluded by ego, he thinks he is the doer. So this is something Bhagavan is trying to clarify, which we have learnt in chapter two, that Purusha is the enabler.
Prakriti functions when Purusha and Prakriti come together. But all actions belong to Prakriti. There is no activity in I, the Purusha that we consider our own self, the I which last time we talked of will and free will.
German philosopher Schopenhauer wrote a book called the World as Will and Representation. So this will is the force which enables the Prakriti to represent itself. So here we are saying the actions are performed in Prakrut.
There is something similar to the situation in my house, where there are several gadgets which generate heat, light, sound, and pictures, which make the house lively and livable. But all this equipment is only functioning when its electrified. So if a bulb somehow gets this ego that I am the one who gives light, then the electricity as the guru can come and tell that bulb, No, no.
All activities are performed by the equipment, but not because of themselves -- because of the electricity functioning through them. But activity does not belong to electricity. Whether the bulb is not functioning well, or is dim or bright -- that does not belong to the electricity; it belongs to the bulb itself. See, the bulb is getting jealous -- That other bulb is brighter, and I am dimmer, and I have to do something to be brighter. All that belongs to Prakriti.
But once its first of all know that you are not the doer. Your dimness or brightness belongs to the equipment and not to you, the electricity. Ahankara Vimudhatma Karta Aham Iti Manyate -- he thinks that he is the doer.
But one who knows the reality, the truth about the gunas and Karma -- Tattva-vit Tu Mahabhaho Guna Karma Vibhagayoh -- he knows the gunas of the Prakriti: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, and their functions. The function of Sattva is existence and knowledge. Rajas is activity and Tamas is inertia.
They have their own gunas, things which are made up of these three gunas in Prakriti. They function according to those gunas and permutation combinations of those gunas. Guna Gunesajjade Knowing that the qualities of my senses and the sense objects outside, when they come together, when the activity takes place, as we have seen last time, that the senses create sensation on the mind, the sensation creates the perception in mind.
That perception conception of that object, that conception of that object. If it is in line with my tendencies, then it creates action. If it is not in line with my tendency, I wont even pay attention.
There are so many sensations come to me, but I am only aware of those I am paying attention to. And I am paying attention to those only which are in line with my tendencies. So Bhagavan says, Guna Guneshu Vartan Tah.
My guna is this limited being and the guna of the objects outside, they are acting with each other, but I remains uninvolved. So the verse we have seen which is almost a summary of Karma Yoga in two lines. Bhagavan says how to practice Karma Yoga.
Mai sarvani Karmani Sanyasya Adhyatma Cheta Saha Nirasi Nirmamo Bhatva Yidyaswa Vigatha Juraha. Renouncing all actions in me with mind centered on yourself. Its like that electricity guru telling the bulb, You offer all your light to me.
It is me who enables you to give light. You just focus on your own self. What is your reality? Nirasi Nirmamo Bhatva. You do not have any expectation what will come out of me.
So dont consider your past achievement is yours. All that was happening for that bulb is because of electricity. As long as electricity is functioning, whether it was giving a good light or a bad light or it was performing according to the expectation of the home owner or not.
All that is because of the electricity. Whatever is coming out of you as actions, devote all of them to me, the enabler. So here the me, as Bhagavan said, is Your own self, your true self which is limitless.
You are binding it into your own limitedness. You offer all your actions to me and do not have any expectations. Do not dwell in future.
What will happen in future? Will my actions generate good results or not? Will I achieve something or not? All that you leave to the Karma Phaladata, the giver of fruits, and remain Nirmamaha. All you accomplished in the past is also past. We have a great tendency, most of the older cultures especially, to dwell in the past and say we used to have a great culture.
Look at our culture in Mahabharata. Look at our culture in Ramas time. That doesnt really matter.
What are you doing right now matters. Your culture right now. Are we the most cultured people on this planet? Do we have the right values or are we corrupt people? That matters what we are doing right now, not what we did in the past.
Not we may do in the future. So Bhagawan said Nirasi Nirmama Bhutva Yudhyasva Vigata Jwaraha. You engage in your activity.
Inactivity is not an option for you. You engage in your activity without having these agitations in your mind which is like a fever will rob your energy. This agitations about what will I get in the future and what are my accomplishments in the past.
Forget about all of that. Become completely healthy to function in present. Thats basically a summary of Karma Yoga.
Act in present, do not worry about the future. Do not regret what you did or did not do or accomplish in the past. And engage yourself in actions.
Devote all actions to the enabler, the self in you. You can only act as long as you are living. You will not be able to act when you die.
After your death, there is no activity for this limited body. So therefore offer all your actions to the enabler, the consciousness, your own self. And then Bhagavan says, Yeme Matamin, this is my opinion whether you like it or not.
But Im telling you, this is my Eme Matamidam Nityam Anuthisthanti Manavah. Those people who follow these teachings of mine. This teaching which I have just taught you, the Karma Yoga, how to act in this world, Offer your actions to the Supreme Self, the supreme will.
Our desire is to live. So there is a will to live, a will to act. Free will is something when I have more choices and I can choose one of them, thats a free will.
If I have a Desire to play outside as a child. But my mother said that you have to do homework. Well if I can decide its a free will.
But if my mother decides then no, no. You can go out to play right now but do your homework. Thats not a free will.
So Bhagavan says that you have free will. You have a very narrow window of free will. Either you can choose my teachings of how to act in this world, or you can follow other opinions about how you can get happiness through your actions.
So we do have a concept in the last time we argued about whether we have concept of free. We do have a concept of free. We call it Purushartha Purushasthana Prarabdha.
Prarabdhdha is something I have no control over. There is no free will there in Prarabdha. The situation Im facing is because of my past actions.
Those past actions go as long as I can think about my existence. This life, previous life, life previous to that, whatever that is. Thats Prarabdha situation is presented to me by my Prarabdha.
The way I act in this situation is my Purushart. I dont have a complete free will that I can do whatever I want Because I cant change the situation. But I do have free will to act within the circumstances.
See, will of an individual is always limited. A complete free will is the universal will. The will of God as we call it in our religious terminology.
Universal will is free. I have a limited free will and I can exercise that free will. So Bhagawan said those who exercise their narrow free will to follow my teachings Eme matamidam nityam Anuthisthati Manava who constantly follow my teachings.
Sraddhavantaha Anusuyantaha muchante tiyapi Karmabhi. Those who follow my teachings with Shraddha without raising trivial doubts it is my opinion that they will also achieve the liberation from Karma Naiskarma Siddhe. They will achieve the final goal.
So here couple of things we can look at. What Bhagavan is saying is that you may have your own doubts whether this is really workable. This Karma Yoga we had been talking about.
Act without any expectations. Dont have any regrets about what you achieved all the way. Unless I have a passion to achieve something.
If I have a fire in my belly to go and get it how am I going to get it? Unless I have this passion to achieve and ILL do anything to achieve it based on my tendencies. Bhagawan said, put all this thing aside. Dont raise those trivial doubts in your mind.
If you subside those trivial doubts in your mind and have Sraddha, have faith that this will work and then you follow all the time. Nityam, Anuti, Sthunti, Manava. Those people who practice, practice that narrow free will to take my advice and have faith in it and follow, they will also be released from all karma, all actions, all sorrows, all unhappiness.
We may have heard before, before Gita came along, there were so many other maths as we have discussed there Sat Dashara, Samari, Swarvadi, Samarani, Swarvadi. Some say going to heaven is the only goal. And others say the liberation is the goal.
There are so many Mata. But I say Krishna says this is my Mata. You may think this is so simplistic.
People say to achieve the Samadhi, Yogi has to practice for a long period of time. And you are saying Samatvam Yoga, Uchathe, just a balanced mind and youre done. So you may have lots of doubts.
But if your faith in my teachings and follow, you shall achieve that nice karma. So we have discussed many times this word Shraddha. Is it the blind faith that Krishna cannot be wrong, that I have to follow him whether I like it or not? We have come across several definitions of Shraddha.
One. He says, my belief in what I do not know, something I do not know. I do not know whether Bhagavan exists or not.
Thats my belief that yes, there is a superior power. Even though I do not know what that power is right now. But I have believed that I may come to know sometime.
If I work at it diligently, I will come to know that power, that supreme power. What I believe in is Shraddha. If I have a belief in something which I do not have direct knowledge of right now, the faith that I will come to know -- then my belief is correct. s Shraddha.
Thats s definition. But Shankaracharyas definition is: Guru Vedanta Vakya Adishu Vishvasah Shraddha -- my trust in the words of my teacher and scriptures. Scriptures in a sense, the books of knowledge which I have trusted.
Upanishads, Vedanta, Bible, whatever you consider book of knowledge, if you have trust in that, thats Sraddha.

Krishna presents here a clear choice with clear consequences. Those who follow His teaching with shraddha (faith) and without anasuya (fault-finding) are freed from the bondage of karma. Those who reject it, carp at it, or fail to practice it are declared nashtan - lost or destroyed, deluded in all their knowledge. Strong words, but Krishna speaks them to emphasize that this is not mere philosophy to debate but a practical path to follow.
The teaching on shraddha deserves special attention. Shraddha is not blind faith but trusting confidence - the willingness to act on a teaching before you have fully verified it through experience. It is like trusting a doctors prescription before the medicine has cured you. Without this initial trust, no experiment can begin. Equally important is being anasuyanto - free from the tendency to find fault, to argue, to resist. This does not mean uncritical acceptance, but rather an open, receptive attitude that allows the teaching to work.
Examine your relationship with these teachings today. Do you approach them with shraddha - a genuine willingness to experiment and experience? Or do you find yourself arguing, doubting, finding reasons why they might not work for you? Notice that Krishna does not ask for blind belief but for sincere practice. He says anutishthanti - those who follow, practice, live by these teachings. Today, choose one principle from Karma Yoga - perhaps acting without attachment to results, or offering your work as Yajna - and practice it with full shraddha, suspending your inner critic for just one day. Let your experience, not your arguments, be the test.
